bib_record_text: Under the direction of Alphonse Morand, Secretary of the Constituent Assembly, the first issue was published on January 1st 1839. It was published three times a week until the end of April that same year and was then replaced by the Echo des Alpes.

bib_record_text: Successor to the conservative Courrier de Sion, the Courrier du Valais appeared from May 10, 1935 to August 4, 1938. Adorned with the same motto, "God and fatherland", which the Gazette du Simplon had adopted in its time, it was published three times a week. It was edited by Fribourg's Leopold Rey, who in 1937 founded the virulent Tribune valaisanne. Fighting radicalism and its "anti-Catholic ideology", the Courrier was also the enemy of socialism, whose dangers for Switzerland and its patriots it regularly reminded people about. It also subscribed to anti-Semitic theses, publishing on August 24, 1936 an article by Mathieu Deigeilh entitled The Jews must pay. This pamphlet was to be followed by several others, in particular in the Page of National Union columns that from August 26, 1936 the Courrier devoted to the Union nationale valaisanne, an organization founded by Valais fascists and frontists.
title: Courrier du Valais

bib_record_text: The first issue of La Sentinelle appeared on January 4th, 1890. Founded by the Union des sociétés ouvrières of La Chaux-de-Fonds with Walter Biolley (1866-1905) as editor, it became the mirror of the Socialist Party’s ideas in 1896. Strongly committed to social justice and the working class, the journal was shaped by political personalities such as Charles Naine (1874-1926) and Ernest-Paul Graber (1875-1956). Often plagued by financial problems, in 1965 it merged with the Vaud and Geneva Socialist daily newspaper Le Peuple and became Le Peuple, La Sentinelle. This eminent French-speaking Socialist daily survived in this form until May 19, 1971, the date of the publication of the last issue.

bib_record_text: L’Essor is an independent newspaper published in French-speaking Switzerland since 1905. Initially published twice monthly, it became monthly in 1973 and from 1994 appeared every two months. The orientation of the newspaper was originally social, moral and religious, and thus reflected the social Christianity movement of its founding pastors, including Paul Pettavel. From 1923-1932, the newspaper moved away from its pacifist position and was renamed Le Nouvel Essor. At the end of this phase, L'Essor returned to its original orientation concerning pacifism, Christian socialism and new pedagogies. Among its editors, L'Essor has included prominent influential figures such as teachers Edouard Claparède and Adolphe Ferrière, Professor Edmond Privat or journalists Eric Descoeudres and René Bovard. L'Essor continues to be published 6 times a year and to defend the universal values of humanism.

bib_record_text: The Bündner Nachrichten followed the Volksfreund using a larger page format. The first issue was published on December 17th, 1885. First it was published three times a week, then from December 18th, 1886 six times a week until 1892. According to an announcement in the last issue of Volksfreund (December 16th, 1885), the Bündner Nachrichten was to be a progressive-democratic organ of news from home and abroad, with editorials covering the major questions of the day and items of general interest. The Bündner Nachrichten were in conflict with Der Freie Rätier which had moved to the right. However in 1892, Manatschal bought Der Freie Rätier and merged it with his own paper. In the end, a newspaper with the long-established title Der Freie Rätier was produced, and it became a significant liberal mouthpiece.
title: Bündner Nachrichten

Die Zeitung erschien 1822 unter dem Titel Neue Zuger-Zeitung (I), 1823-1831 unter Zuger-Zeitung und 1832-1849 unter Der freie Schweizer. Die Zeitung erschien wöchentlich. Zuerst unpolitisch, entwickelte sie sich ab Ende 1820er Jahre zum liberalen Meinungsblatt. Als letztes Nachfolgeblatt der ersten in Zug gedruckten Zeitung erlag Der freie Schweizer Ende 1949 der starken parteiinternen Konkurrenz der seit Anfang gleichen Jahres neu erscheinenden Zeitung Zugerisches Kantons-Blatt. In dieser Onlineversion sind die Jahrgänge von 1814 bis 1849 enthalten. (1822 Neue Zuger Zeitung (I), 1823 - 1831 Zuger Zeitung, 1832 - 1849 Der freie Schweizer)

bib_record_text: The Volksfreund was issued from January 8th, 1879 to December 16th, 1885. In the sample number of December 28th, 1878, it was announced that the Volksfreund would appear twice a week (Tuesday and Saturday) with the slogan "for the people rights - against all evil" and would report on the everyday social and economic conditions of the people. The Volksfreund positioned itself as a support, friend, advisor and spokesman of the people, the little people, and wanted to report independently on world events. In 1882, the Volksfreund was issued with the motto "everything for and by the people", stressing that the true democracy in which all people form a social body, could only come about through the participation of the entire people in the legislative process. From January 1st, 1882 the Volksfreund was published daily. The Volksfreund was politically to the left and reported in a distinctive and incisive manner on local and Graubünden matters, with shorter reports on other cantons and abroad. Amusing items were also included. In the issue appearing December 16th, 1885 (no. 100) it was announced that from the following day the Volksfreund would appear under the title Bündner Nachrichten as a progressive-democratic mouthpiece with Manatschal as editor.The online version of the Volksfreund for 1882 is incomplete as there are issues missing from the print collection.
title: Der Volksfreund

bib_record_text: From 20.12.1847, the Eidgenössische Zeitung resumed publication,following the resignation of the previous editorial committee directed by Caspar Heinrich Schulthess (1815-1885). The editor-in-chief, Johann Bernhard Spyri (1821-1884), who was in charge from March 1848, brought along a more moderate attitude. On 1.7.1860 he handed over responsibility to Alexander von Tavel (1827-1900), who subsequently published the newspaper at the new headquarters in Bern, until its final issue on 30.6.1864.
title: Der Erzähler

bib_record_text: The newspaper was founded in 1863. It was first published in 1864, initially on a twice-weekly basis, under the title Freiburger-Zeitung und Anzeiger für die westliche Schweiz and then from 1904, under a new title Freiburger Nachrichten und Anzeiger für die westliche Schweiz. The Freiburger Nachrichten is the only German-language daily newspaper in the canton of Fribourg. From 1973 it opened up both on a political and religious level. Today, the publication deals mainly with local and regional news. The supra-regional pages are adapted from the Berner Zeitung.
title: Freiburger Nachrichten

bib_record_text: From January 1799 through to December 1801, during the Helvetic Republic Johann Jakob Hausknecht published a quarto format weekly paper aimed as a political struggle against the aristocrats. The first year (1799) contained 34 issues with a total of 256 pages, the second and third years (1800, 1801) each contained 52 issues with 432 and 482 pages respectively.
title: Der helvetische Volksfreund

subtitles: Tägliche Bündner Zeitung
founder: Johann Carl von Tscharner together with friends
bib_record_text: After a sample issue on December 29th, 1847, the Liberale Alpenbote was published from January 1st, 1848 to June 30th, 1860 twice a week (Wednesday and Saturday), from New Year 1852 three times a week (Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday) and finally, from 1857 six times a week. The Liberale Alpenbote was founded by Johann Carl von Tscharner together with friends. As editor, Tscharner actively took part in discussions on important issues around the legislative structure of the new canton and gave constructive suggestions for its implementation. Tscharner also catered for cultural interests by including in each number a very good feature with non-political stories, instructive stories or literary news. The Liberale Alpenbote was soon counted among the most important political institutions and became a newspaper of national importance. Following Planta’s resignation in 1856, the "liberale Alpenbote" quickly went downhill, and despite several transformations and editorial changes it finally ceased publication with the last issue appearing on June 30th, 1860. It was followed by the Bündnerische Wochenzeitung published by L. Hitz with PC von Planta as editor.
title: Der Liberale Alpenbote

bib_record_text: La Liberté is a French-language Swiss daily newspaper published in Fribourg. It is published 6 times a week, from Monday through to Saturday. Founded in 1871, the property of St. Paul SA in Fribourg, La Liberté is one of the last Swiss-French daily newspapers to be completely independent of major media groups. Its subtitle has changed several times: Journal catholique quotidien, L'ami du peuple, Quotidien politique, religieux, social, Quotidien du matin, Quotidien romand édité à Fribourg.
title: La Liberté

subtitles: Eine Volkszeitung für Graubünden
bib_record_text: After three sample issues on December 11th, 18th and 25th , 1841 (all no. 1), the Morgenstern was published from January 1st, 1842 (No. 1) to September 26th, 1843 (no. 77) twice a week (Tuesday and Saturday, then from no. 52, July 1st, 1843 on Friday instead of Saturday). The Morgenstern was printed in quarto format by the Sutter brothers in Chur. The publisher was Ludwig Christ, who was dismissed from the editorial board of the Bündner Zeitung due to disagreements with S. Benedict and wanted to create with the Morgenstern a fierce rival newspaper. The subtitle a Volkszeitung für Graubünden indicates that Christ turned towards the ordinary citizen. He wrote for the cause of the farmer and the improvement of the middle class. The Morgenstern contained reports on the Confederation, on Graubünden, on other cantons and information from abroad. The enthusiastic participation of the people in the contents of the Morgenstern was illustrated by Christ through numerous real or fictitious entries from various valleys.
title: Der Morgenstern

predecessor_acronym: 1874: Neues Tag- und Anzeigeblatt aus der östlichen Schweiz
bib_record_text: The Catholic-Conservative paper Neuen Tagblatts aus der östlichen Schweiz [New daily paper from Eastern Switzerland] was published from 1.7.1856 to 30.6.1874 with an interruption from 5.7 through to 3.10.1871. The four-page newspaper appeared six times a week and from 1874 was titled Neues Tag- und Anzeigeblatt aus der östlichen Schweiz.[New daily and official announcements paper from Eastern Switzerland]. Until the end of 1857 and from the middle of 1870 advertisements were also published. The Neue Tagblatt aus der östlichen Schweiz was the successor to the Wahrheitsfreunds and the precursor to the Ostschweiz. This online version contains the years 1856 to 1873.
title: Neues Tagblatt aus der östlichen Schweiz

bib_record_text: The Neue Zuger Zeitung (II) was published weekly from 03 March 1846 to 31 December1891, and twice a week from 1869 onwards. It was produced in Zug by the printing works of Alois Keiser (1820-1849), and Johann Baptist Elsener (1825-1910) published the newspaper from 1855 to 1891 after having taken over the printing works. The newspaper was politically conservative. This online version contains the publications from 1846 to 1891.
title: Neue Zuger Zeitung (II)

bib_record_text: The liberal St. Galler Zeitung was founded by Jakob Friedrich Wartmann and was published from January 3rd 1831 until December 31st 1881 with each issue containing four pages. For the last 30 years of its publication it was the mouthpiece of the St. Gallen liberals. Publication frequency varied over the years. From January 7th 1846 to June 30th 1851 it was titled St. Galler-Bote.
title: St.Galler Zeitung

subtitles: enthaltend die neuesten Begebenheiten der löblichen Stände Zürich, Bern, Basel, Thurgäu und Rheinthal
bib_record_text: In the year of transition 1798, from 15. To 11.7 the bookseller Johann Jakob Hausknecht produced the quarto format newspaper titled Schweizerische Tag-Blätter, enthaltend die neuesten Begebenheiten der Löblichen Stände Zürich, Bern, Basel, Thurgäu und Rheinthal (title page of the first collection)[Swiss daily containing the latest events from the worthy places Zurichm Bern, Basel, Thurgäu und Rheinthal] enthaltend die neuesten Begebheiten der Löblichen Stände Zürich, Bern, Basel, Luzern, Solothurn, Schaffhausen und Thurgäu (title page of the second collection) [containing the latest events from the worthy places Zürich, Bern, Basel, Luzern, Solothurn, Schaffhausen and Thurgäu] oder die merkwürdigen Ereignisse in der jetzigen Staats-Umwälzung vom May 1798 bis zu Anfang Julii (title page of the thrid collection) [or the strange events in the present state of upheaval May 1798 to the beginning of July] was published. The title Schweizerische Tag-Blätter appeared at the head of each number only after the second collection. It appeared irregularly in January and from February onwards twice a week.
title: Schweizerische Tag-Blätter

bib_record_text: This four page newspaper from the St. Gallen Catholic Conservatives was published from 2.1.1835 until 24.12.1863 under the title Der St. Gallische Wahrheitsfreund, shortened to Der Wahrheitsfreund ("The Friend of Truth") from 1844 onwards. From 1835 it appeared once a week (on Fridays), from 12.10 until 30.12.1847 twice weekly (Tuesdays and Fridays) and then once more as a weekly until 24.12.1863. Founded before the St. Galler Tagblatt (1839), it was the main Catholic-Conservative newspaper of the time in St. Gallen canton and the precursor of the Neuen Tagblatts aus der östlichen Schweiz [New daily paper from Eastern Switzerland] (1856) as well as its successor the Ostschweiz [Eastern Switzerland].
title: Der Wahrheitsfreund

bib_record_text: The Zugerbieter (I) was published weekly from 12 December 1865 to 29 December 1868 at J. (later Johann) Baptist Elsener in Zug. The newspaper was conservative in approach, its subtitle defined it as "the nephew of the Neuer Zuger-Zeitung" (Vetter zur Neuen Zuger-Zeitung) and a "weekly paper containing advertisements and entertainment" (wöchentliches Anzeige- und Unterhaltungsblatt) . The Zugerbieter was absorbed by the Neue Zuger-Zeitung (II) after 1868.
title: Der Zugerbieter

bib_record_text: This biweekly from the district of Sierre was published on Wednesdays and Saturdays, from July 2, 1902 to June 27, 1903. Every Saturday, it included the official bulletin as a supplement. A newspaper of announcements and information, it devoted itself almost exclusively to news of the district and the canton.
title: La Contrée

subtitles: Wochenpost der Sieben Unabhängigen
bib_record_text: Die Tat wurde 1939 von Gottlieb Duttweiler gegründet und erschien täglich. Sie vertrat insbesondere die Themen des Landesrings der Unabhängigen, einer ebenfalls von Duttweiler gegründeten liberalen Partei. Durch ihre klare politische Haltung - sie distanzierte sich bereits sehr früh vom Nationalsozialismus - und mithilfe ihrer wöchtenlich erscheinenden Beilage Literarische Tat, galt sie mit den Jahren als seriöse Zeitung. Die Literarische Tat wurde von Max Rychner und später von Erwin Jaeckle geleitet. In ihrer besten Zeit, vor dem 2. Weltkrieg, wurde sie in einer Auflage von über 40'000 Exemplaren herausgegeben. Nach Jahren der wachsenden Verluste, die mit der schrumpfenden Bedeutung der politischen Presse einherging, wurde sie 1977 schliesslich eingestellt. Die darauf folgende, von der Migros herausgegebene und von Roger Schawinsky geleitete Boulevardzeitung trug den gleichen Titel und erschien nur noch bis 1978.
title: Die Tat

subtitles: La FCTA : organo della Federazione svizzera dei lavatori del commercio, dei trasporti e dell'alimentazione
bib_record_text: Italienischsprachige Gewerkschaftszeitung sozialdemokratischer Ausrichtung. Offizielles Organ der Federazione svizzera dei lavatori del commercio, dei trasporti e dell'alimentazione. Die Zeitung im Folio-Format erschien wöchentlich und umfasste je vier Seiten. Sie wurde in Bellinzona gedruckt (Tipografia Leins & Vescovi) und wurde 1964 dem neuen Gewerkschaftstitel I diritti del lavoro einverleibt.
title: La FCTA

bib_record_text: La Gazette du Valais naît en 1855 et entend rassembler tous les hommes de bien, quel que soit leur parti politique. Parmi ses objectifs figure la volonté de défendre les droits de l’Eglise et du clergé ; c’est un journal catholique conservateur. La Gazette du Valais paraîtra jusqu’en 1922, après avoir brièvement pris le nom de Nouvelle Gazette du Valais entre 1874 et 1888.
title: Gazette du Valais / Nouvelle gazette du Valais

bib_record_text: With the motto "God and Fatherland", the ultraconservative Gazette du Simplon’s first issue was published on June 25, 1842. From the outset it marked its opposition to the government and the liberal party as well as its attachment "to the Catholic, Apostolic and Roman religion". Often controversial and virulent, it is forced to stop its activities when on April 12, 1843, after the publication of a parody of the assembly of the Jeune Suisse in Saint-Maurice, its printing press was ransacked by a hundred people. On August 31, 1844, La Voix du Rhône succeeded it, but ceased publication after only one issue. The Gazette du Simplon was reborn on November 6, 1844. It now supported the fights of the conservative and clerical government against the attacks of the radical press. It was last published on November 13, 1847, and disappeared definitively during the Sonderbund War after the publication, from November 16 to 24, of four Bulletin de la Gazette du Simplon.
title: Gazette du Simplon

subtitles: Organe officiel de la Fédération suisse des travailleurs de la métallurgie et de l'horlogerie (FTMH)
bib_record_text: Union newspaper of socialist orientation, official organ of the Fédération suisse des ouvriers sur métaux [Swiss Federation of Metal Workers] (from 03.6.1915 with the addition: et horlogers). The title was published every two weeks, initially in quarto format, then from 04.07.1908 in folio format. From 1906-1915 it was printed in Bern (Unionsdruckerei), then from 1916 La Chaux-de-Fonds (Imprimerie coopérative). In 1920 it changed its name: Le Métallurgiste became La Lutte syndicale. The newspaper had several supplements: A l'ouvrière (monthly, 02.02.1929-24.03.1931), La Technique (23.02.1929-15.08.1936), La Page de l'ouvrière (28.03.1931-25.12.1946), La Page des jeunes (20.10.1934-20.06.1936), La Page de la famille (from 06.01.1947). Continued by L'événement syndical (UNIA) from issue Year 79, 1 (28 April 1998). Editors included Achille Graber, Charles Hubacher and Achille Grospierre.
title: La lutte syndicale

subtitles: das Magazin der Gewerkschaft Textil, Chemie, Papier
bib_record_text: A trade union newspaper of social democratic alignment. The Appenzeller weavers’ newspaper was the official organ of the Allgemeiner Verband der Seidenbeuteltuch-Weberei and the Appenzellischer Weberverband and was printed in folio format (Rheineck: Albert Indermaur). Its successor titles were the Ostschweizerische Industrie-Zeitung (1901-1904, printed in quarto, Albert Indermaur in Rheineck) and from 1904 the Textilarbeiter (Organ des Allgemeinen Schweizerischen Textil-Arbeiter-Verbandes. Zur Wahrung der Interessen aller in der Textilbranche beschäftigten Arbeiter und Arbeiterinnen, der Spinner, Weber, Handsticker, Schifflisticker, Wirker, Flechter, Färber, Drucker, Bleicher, Appretierer etc. und der Hilfsarbeiter), 1916-1919 and 1941 in quarto, otherwise in folio, printed 1904-1906 in Rheineck at A Indermaur, 1906-1910 in Zurich (Conzett & Cie), 1910-1928 in Bern (Unionsdruckerei), from 1929 in Zurich (Genossenschaftsdruckerei)), from 1981 in Glattbrugg (Th. Maag AG), from 1984 in Basel (Volksdruckerei). Published monthly, from 1901 onwards every two weeks, editors included Howard Eugster-Züst (Hundwil), Ernst Marti (Zurich), Giacomo Wolf (Zurich), Leo Loew (Basel) Supplements: Die Arbeit, Stimme der Arbeit (ab 1939), Ouvrier de l'industrie textile chimie papier STFV / FOTF, Journal officiel de la fédération suisse des ouvriers du textile et de fabrique (18.06.1946-24.04.1947, ed: Albert Heyer). Until 2001 continued by Neue Gewerkschaft, then until 2004 by the GBI-Zeitung. Absorbed by the magazine Work.
title: Die Gewerkschaft

bib_record_text: Produced by the spa, this monthly appeared from May 15, 1882 to July 1, 1884, and was "created for local interest," in its own words. Addressed to tourists and patients wishing to heal themselves in thermal waters, it devoted most of its pages to the benefits of the resort’s water and to local tourism through articles that were often very comprehensive and specialized.
title: Journal de Saxon

subtitles: Organe de Fédération suisse des ouvriers du commerce, des transports et de l'alimentation
bib_record_text: Union newspaper of social democratic character. Official organ of the Fédération suisse des travailleurs du commerce, des transports et de l'alimentation. The white papers dealt with economic and socio-political topics. The newspaper was published bi-monthly in folio format. It was printed in La Chaux-de-Fonds (Imprimerie coopérative) and included various supplements: A l'Ouvrière (1929-March 1931), La Technique (February 1929-August 1936), Journal syndical édité par l'Union syndicale (November 1932-June 1938), Les Droits du travail (July 1938-), Science et technique (September 1936-30 November 1946), La Page de la famille (07.12.1946-07.06.1947). Pierre Aragno was one of the editors. The title L'Alimentation was published from 01.07.1909-16.04.1910 and La Solidarité from 01.07.1916-29.12.1917 in quarto format. L'Alimentation, Le Prolétaire and La Solidarité also contained articles in Italian (partly under the heading La Solidarietà). It was absorbed into the L'événement syndical.
title: Solidarité

bib_record_text: Association journal of socialist or social democratic colouring. Official organ of the Schweizerische Metallarbeiter-Verband [Swiss Metalworkers' Federation] (since 03.07.1915: Offizielles Organ des Schweiz. Metall- und Uhrenarbeiterverbandes [Official organ of the Swiss Metalworkers' and Watchmakers' Association]). Printed in folio format, initially monthly, then twice weekly from 1903-1904, then weekly from 30.07.1904. The title contains various supplements, including: Aus Technik und Leben (later: Die technische Seite), Unterhaltung und Wissen, Die Arbeit (later: Stimme der Arbeit), Helfer für Garten und Feld. The editors and contributors were well-known trade unionists such as Oskar Schneeberger, Karl Dürr, Konrad Ilg, Peter Bratschi, Fritz Marbach and Ernst Reinhard. Continued by Work.
title: SMUV-Zeitung

title: La Voix du Rhône

subtitles: Gewerkschaft Verkauf, Handel, Transport, Lebensmittel (VHTL)
predecessor_until_date: Korrespondenzblatt des Verbandes der Lebens- und Genussmittelarbeiter der Schweiz, Der Proletarier, Solidarität, VHTL
bib_record_text: Trade union newspaper of social democratic colouring; Organ of the central association that covered workers employed in the food and beverage industry as well as in the trade and transport industry, official organ of the Verband der Handels-, Transport- und Lebensmittelarbeiter der Schweiz [Association of Trade, Transport and Food Workers of Switzerland]. The Korrespondenzblatt initially appeared in quarto format (until 01.08.1907), then in folio format. The publication was initially published every two weeks, then weekly from 06.07.1929. The newspaper was initially printed in the Unionsdruckerei Bern, then from 18.07.1926 in the Genossenschaftsdruckerei Zürich. In the years 1918-1919, in addition to the Stimme der Arbeit, it was accompanied by the supplement Solidarité - Institutions de la Fédération suisse des ouvriers du commerce, transport and de l'alimentation. The French-language journal temporarily did not appear separately. The editors were among others Johann Müller, Hermann Leuenberger, E. Wyss, Jean Schifferstein. Contributions by Wilhelm Liebknecht, Herman Greulich and Robert Grimm also appeared in the Proletarier (1909-1915). It was absorbed into Work.
title: VHTL-Zeitung
